historical_record.description: The Anza Branch Library, opened in 1932, closed on March 14, 2001 for the modernization of its wiring and was expected to reopen in July 2001.
In March 2008 the library set out plans to renovate, seismically strengthen and extend at the rear the Anza Branch Library, then 76 years old, with work expected from 2009 to 2011.

The Board of Education told the library trustees that the westerly half of the old Lafayette School lot, facing 37th Avenue near Anza Street, had been transferred to them for a branch library, the title staying with the Board of Education.
The library trustees appointed John Reid Jr. architect of the new branch library to be built on 37th Avenue near Anza Street, in the Park-Presidio district.
The library trustees approved John Reid Jr.'s preliminary sketches for the new branch library on 37th Avenue at Anza Street.
At a special meeting called to let the general contract for the new branch on 37th Avenue near Anza Street, the library trustees awarded it to Frank J. Reilly, out of about twenty bids.
The Library Commission's branch committee reported that the Anza Branch had been built with money left over from the building fund of the Main Library, half of which Andrew Carnegie had given.
